messages:
maria: Heads up from load test — we hit a mid-stream failover that left clients with a truncated stream and no way to resume.
ashok: Which path failed? egress or upstream?
ben: Upstream probe. Canary region; we flipped routing and gave a 1s drain. Runtime closed connection; frontdoor cut over immediately. Client saw half the response and then connection reset.
maria: We need a repeatable strategy: either frontdoor produces a continuation token at handoff, or runtime must regularly emit checkpoints. Tradeoffs?
sam: Runtime emission is cleaner: it knows token semantics and safe checkpoints (e.g., kv-cache boundaries). Frontdoor can't infer token semantics reliably.
nashok: True, but frontdoor can still emit an opaque continuation (byte-offset + hash) when doing a handoff so reconnection has a chance. Not perfect but better than nothing in extreme fast-failovers.
eva: That would tightly couple frontdoor to resume semantics. Future model formats could break this.
ben: How about hybrid: runtime emits semantic checkpoints when possible; frontdoor only emits opaque continuation on forced handoffs. Runtime offers a validation endpoint to accept the opaque token.
maria: Sketching behavior: 1) runtime optionally emits semantic markers. 2) frontdoor always keeps last-seen byte offset and can fabricate X-Resume-Opaque: base64(offset|sha256). 3) on reconnection, frontdoor POSTs /_resume_validate with header; runtime replies 200 to accept or 409 to reject.
sam: Need to define TTL for continuation tokens and a replay protection mechanism. Also metrics: resume_attempts, resume_success, resume_failures.
nashok: Also need clear error codes: 409 (mismatch), 428 (resume required but impossible), 502 (hard fail). Frontdoor must choose whether to retry against original runtime or fail fast.
eva: Security: tokens must be HMAC-signed per-tenant. For hosted deployments, use Redwood KMS; dedicated/private can use customer-managed keys.
ben: Side-effects note: if route mutates state (DB writes, webhooks), resuming might duplicate effects. We should classify routes with a side_effects property: none/managed/visible. Frontdoor should only auto-retry if side_effects==none or managed with idempotency markers.
maria: Trailers: if runtime emits final-status trailers mid-stream then resuming is impossible. We should change runtime to delay final trailers until final completion.
sam: For compatibility, add route-level flag legacy_trailers that disables resume if clients depend on them. We'll need migration docs.
nashok: Observability: add tracing spans frontdoor.resume.prepare, frontdoor.resume.validate, runtime.resume.accept. Console metrics + logs for debugging.
eva: Rollout plan: feature-flagged switch, canary in one region, add console charts, then opt-in per-route before global.
ben: I'll draft an RFC with sequence diagrams and exact header shapes. We'll include sample lifecycle: graceful handoff vs forced failover.
ci-bot: Reminder: add feature flag resume-handoff to deploy checklist.
maria: Schedule sync tomorrow 10:30 to finalize API surfaces and error semantics.
eva: I'll prepare compatibility matrix.
sam: I'll prototype /_resume_validate behavior and TTL.
maria: Great. End thread.
